title: Handshaking induction: the base case of the induction on edges

located_defect.description: In the base case of its induction on the number of edges the source asserts (stored source line 0009) that a graph without edges has one vertex or none. As a universal statement over finite simple graphs this is the located defect. Supply the one hypothesis on G, drawn from the source's context, under which the sentence becomes true, prove the corrected sentence for every finite simple graph, show the hypothesis is neither empty nor trivially true on edgeless graphs, and prove the handshake lemma SourceGoal the source is after.

namespace SE_math_782216_q_Census

-- ===== FIXED PART: only the hole «HOLE» may be edited =====
/-- The hypothesis to add to the source's base-case sentence: a condition on the graph `G` drawn from
the source's context (connectivity). The hole must be a proposition about `G` in Mathlib vocabulary; it
may not mention the number of vertices (`Fintype.card`, `Subsingleton`, ...), edge counts or `BaseClaim`. -/
def guard {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop := «HOLE»

/-- The corrected base-case sentence: under the added hypothesis, a finite simple graph without edges has
at most one vertex (shape fixed). -/
def CorrectedBaseClaim : Prop :=
